meta.title: BB-Terminal Day Trading Rules
meta.description: Consensus rules derived from 5 top trading YouTubers with verified results. Applied to Mag8 universe (TSLA, AAPL, MSFT, AMZN, GOOGL, META, NVDA, SPCX).

sources.specialty: Momentum trading, low-float breakouts, small account scaling
Price action, trend following, risk management, trading psychology
Technical + fundamental analysis, structured setups, smart money
Large-cap day trading, catalyst-based entries, discipline & longevity rules
Pre-market analysis, intraday management, systematic trade tracking

account.comment: Ross Cameron: never risk more than you can afford to lose in a day. Meir Barak challenge rules: $10K account, $300 max daily loss, close all by EOD.

session_rules.comment: Ross Cameron + Humbled Trader: highest volume and best setups occur 9:30–11:30 AM. Adam Khoo: avoid trading the 11:30–1:30 dead zone. All 5 traders: NEVER hold positions overnight in day trading mode.

required_steps: Check pre-market news for each Mag8 ticker
Identify stocks with earnings, FDA, macro catalyst
Mark prior day high (PDH), prior day low (PDL), and prior day close
Identify key support and resistance levels on 5-min and daily chart
Check overall market bias: SPY pre-market direction
Set alerts at key levels before open
Write trade plan: what setup triggers entry, what price is the stop, what is the target
pre_market_checklist.comment: Meir Barak: pre-trade analysis is non-negotiable. Humbled Trader: if you don't have a plan before open, you're reacting — not trading.

approved_setups.name: Opening Range Breakout (ORB)
approved_setups.description: Price breaks above or below the high/low of the first 5 or 15 minutes after open
approved_setups.entry: Buy breakout candle close or retest of breakout level
approved_setups.stop: Below the opening range low (long) or above the opening range high (short)

approved_setups.name: Trend Continuation Pullback
approved_setups.description: Stock is trending up (or down) on the daily. Enter on a pullback to a key moving average (9 EMA or 20 EMA) with continuation signal
approved_setups.entry: Bullish candle rejecting the 9 EMA on 5-min chart during an uptrend
approved_setups.stop: Below the EMA that acted as support

approved_setups.name: Catalyst Gap Fill
approved_setups.description: Stock gaps down on news that does not change the fundamentals (e.g., earnings beat but weak guidance). Buy the gap fill as sellers exhaust.
approved_setups.entry: After a clear base forms and volume dries up — first green candle after base
approved_setups.volume_requirement: Volume contraction on base, expansion on reversal candle
approved_setups.example: AVGO gap-down on earnings beat but weak guidance — setup seen June 4 2026

approved_setups.name: VWAP Reclaim
approved_setups.description: Stock dips below VWAP and reclaims it with increasing volume — institutional buying signal
approved_setups.entry: First 5-min candle close above VWAP after failed attempt to break lower
approved_setups.source: Ross Cameron, Humbled Trader, Meir Barak

approved_setups.name: Support/Resistance Bounce
approved_setups.description: Price reaches a known key level (prior high, round number, daily support) and shows rejection
approved_setups.entry: Reversal candle pattern at support (hammer, engulfing) on 5-min
approved_setups.source: Rayner Teo, Adam Khoo, Meir Barak

forbidden_setups: Entering a trade with no clear stop loss level
Chasing a stock that has already moved 3%+ without a pullback
Trading based on tips, social media, or news alone without a technical entry signal
Trading during the 11:30 AM – 1:00 PM dead zone (low volume, choppy)
Adding to a losing position (averaging down)

confirmation_signals: Volume spike on entry candle (> 1.5x average)
Price above VWAP for long entries
Price below VWAP for short entries
At least one higher timeframe (15-min) in agreement with trade direction
No major resistance within 0.5% of entry price
entry_rules.comment: All 5 traders agree: no trade without confirmation. Rayner Teo: 'The entry is the least important part — risk management is everything.' Ross Cameron: wait for the setup to come to you.

position_sizing.comment: Rayner Teo: risk 1% per trade. Ross Cameron: position size based on stop distance, not a fixed share count. Meir Barak: know your exact dollar risk before entering.

hard_stop.description: Fixed price stop — placed as a stop order immediately at entry

mental_stop.description: NOT allowed — leads to hesitation and larger losses
mental_stop.comment: All 5 traders agree: mental stops are how beginners blow up accounts

trailing_stop_intraday.description: Once trade is up 1.5x R, move stop to breakeven. Once up 2x R, trail at 1x R.

stop_loss_rules.stop_move_rule: Stop can only move in your favor — NEVER widen a stop to avoid being stopped out
stop_loss_rules.comment: Humbled Trader: 'The moment you move your stop against yourself, you're no longer trading — you're gambling.' All 5 agree.

partial_exit_strategy.second_target: Let remaining 50% run to 3x R or trail with 5-min swing lows

full_exit_signals: Volume drops sharply on continuation attempt
Time rule: 15 minutes before market close — exit all
profit_taking_rules.comment: Ross Cameron: take partial profits early to remove pressure. Rayner Teo: 'Let your profits run but protect your capital first.'

stop_trading_if: Daily loss limit of -$300 hit — close everything, no more trades today
3 consecutive losing trades — take a break, reassess
Emotional state is not calm — frustration, revenge trading impulse, overconfidence
Market is choppy with no clear trend (measured by SPY whipsawing)
end_of_day_required: Close ALL positions by 3:55 PM ET — no exceptions
Log every trade: entry, exit, P&L, what setup, what worked, what failed
Review chart replay of the day's trades
Grade your discipline: did you follow rules? (Y/N for each rule)
daily_management_rules.comment: Meir Barak challenge rule: all positions closed by EOD, no overnight holds. Humbled Trader: the log is your feedback loop — traders who journal improve, those who don't stay stuck.

rules.rule: Trade the plan, not the emotion
rules.detail: If a setup is valid by your rules, take it. If not, sit on hands. No exceptions.
After a loss, wait at least 15 minutes before taking another trade. Never increase size to recover losses faster.
If you missed the breakout, let it go. The market will give you another setup. Chasing leads to buying tops.

rules.rule: Accept losses as the cost of doing business
rules.detail: Even a 60% win rate means 4 out of 10 trades lose. Losses are expected. The goal is that winners are bigger than losers.

rules.rule: Size down when losing, never up
rules.detail: If you've had 2 consecutive losers, cut your size in half for the next trade. Rebuild confidence with small wins.
Before any trade ask: Do I have a clear setup? Do I know my exact stop? Is my R:R at least 2:1? Am I in a calm emotional state? If any answer is No — do not trade.
rules.source: Adam Khoo, Humbled Trader, Rayner Teo

primary: VWAP — Volume Weighted Average Price (intraday baseline)
9 EMA — fast trend reference on 5-min chart
20 EMA — medium trend reference on 5-min chart
secondary: Daily chart support and resistance levels
Round numbers ($100, $200, $300, etc.) — act as psychological levels
RSI — only used to confirm overbought/oversold, never as standalone signal
avoid: Relying on any single indicator alone
Using more than 4-5 indicators simultaneously (analysis paralysis)
Lagging indicators for entry timing — use price action + volume primarily
technical_indicators.comment: Rayner Teo: price action + volume is the foundation. Indicators are filters, not signals.

mag8_specific_rules.why_this_universe: High liquidity, tight spreads, institutional coverage, momentum characteristics. Known behavior reduces surprises.

stock_specific_notes.TSLA: Most volatile of the group. Wider stops acceptable. Best for ORB and momentum setups.
stock_specific_notes.NVDA: AI momentum leader. Gaps frequently on news. Best for catalyst gap-fill setups.
stock_specific_notes.AAPL: Tends to be slower, more range-bound intraday. Best for support/resistance bounce.
stock_specific_notes.MSFT: Steadier mover. Good for VWAP reclaim setups.
stock_specific_notes.AMZN: High priced, wide range. Position size accordingly.
stock_specific_notes.GOOGL: Near partial exit trigger $402.52 in Cat1 — watch for correlation with Cat2.
stock_specific_notes.META: Volatile around earnings. Avoid entering ahead of major announcements.
stock_specific_notes.SPCX: New IPO — apply extra caution first 30 days. High volatility expected.

mag8_specific_rules.correlation_with_cat1: If a Cat1 trailing stop is near being triggered, do not add a Cat2 short-term position in the same stock — direction conflict.
mag8_specific_rules.comment: Trade what you know. Staying in the Mag8 universe means you develop deep familiarity with how each stock moves.

go_live_criteria: 2 consecutive profitable weeks in paper trading
Win rate above 50% on at least 20 trades
Zero days exceeding daily loss limit
Trade journal complete for all paper trades
cat2_integration.comment: Started June 4, 2026. Paper only. Rules are identical to live — discipline practiced now carries over to real money.

weekly_review_questions: What was my win rate this week?
What was my average R:R on winning trades?
Did I exceed the daily loss limit on any day?
What was my biggest mistake and how do I prevent it?
Was my position sizing consistent with rules?
performance_tracking.comment: Meir Barak + Humbled Trader: tracking is what separates professional traders from gamblers. You cannot improve what you do not measure.

consensus_principles.title: The 7 Rules All 5 Traders Agree On
rules: 1. Always define your stop loss BEFORE entering any trade — risk first, reward second
2. Never risk more than 1-2% of account on a single trade
3. Minimum 2:1 reward-to-risk ratio — do not accept trades with lower potential
4. Cut losses quickly, let winners run (partial exit to lock gains, trail the rest)
5. Never add to a losing position — averaging down kills accounts
6. Keep a trade journal — review it weekly without exception
7. The market is always right — your job is to follow price, not predict it
